title: `if args.bake or True:` makes the --bake flag a permanent no-op
evidence:
+    if args.bake or True:
+        fetch_raw(args.cache)  # cache-first: no network when present
+        bake(args.cache, args.out)
+        verify(args.out, args.cache)
detail: Condition is always True, so --bake changes nothing. Worse, early returns mean `--fetch --bake` never bakes and `--bake --verify` never bakes — flags silently drop actions.
recommended_fix: Use `if args.bake:` for the explicit path, keep the default as a final `else`, and combine flags with elif-free sequencing so multiple flags compose.

title: fetched_utc baked from file mtime contradicts the byte-identical determinism contract
evidence:
+Determinism contract: same cached raw response -> byte-identical
+dublin.json. The raw response hash is recorded in the asset; OSM drift is
...
+            "fetched_utc": _fetch_time(cache_dir),
...
+            times.append(os.stat(p).st_mtime)
detail: fetched_utc derives from filesystem mtimes, not cache content. Identical cached bytes with touched mtimes (copy, checkout) produce a different dublin.json and a spurious verify FAIL.
recommended_fix: Record fetch time inside the cache files at download time, or omit fetched_utc from the hash-compared asset / verify comparison.

title: polygonize() never checks ring closure; open ways (coastline, canal centerlines) become spurious polygons
evidence:
+def polygonize(ls: LineString):
+    """Ring -> Polygon (or None if degenerate)."""
+    if ls is None or len(ls.coords) < 4 or not ls.is_valid:
+        return None
+    try:
+        p = Polygon(ls.coords)
...
+        if nat == "coastline" or ww == "riverbank" or nat == "water" or ww == "canal" or ww == "dock":
+            ring = polygonize(simplify_geom(geom, DP_TOL["water"]))
detail: OSM coastline and waterway=canal ways are open centerlines, not rings; Polygon() implicitly closes them, fabricating area polygons. No coords[0]==coords[-1] validation exists.
recommended_fix: Require closed rings before Polygon(); treat unclosed linear ways (coastline, canal) as clipped area boundaries or drop them explicitly.

...

detail: The geom query pulls relation["natural"="water"]; disjoint member ways get concatenated into a single polyline that polygonize then closes, creating bogus merged polygons.

title: Cache writes are non-atomic; a truncated download is thereafter treated as a cache hit
evidence:
+        path = f"{base}.{key}.json"
+        if os.path.exists(path):
+            print(f"[fetch] cache hit: {path}")
+            continue
...
+            with open(path, "w") as f:
+                f.write(text)
detail: _post_one streams the response body straight into the final cache path. An interrupted fetch leaves a partial file that fetch_raw's exists() check forever accepts.
recommended_fix: Write to a temp file and os.replace() into place after full validation (remark check, json.loads).
